chunks: We have determined the stations of the moon, so that (after its wanderings) it returns as a dried up inflorescent spike of dates.

key_terms.الْعُرْجُونِ: Inflorescent spike/stalk of a date palm
key_terms.الْقَدِيمِ: The old/dried (referring to the waning crescent)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'returned as the dried up inflorescent spike of dates' mean in Surah Yaseen?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores Allah’s absolute sovereignty over celestial mechanics, serving as a tangible sign (ayah) of the Resurrection and the precision of divine decree. The metaphor of the 'old palm stalk' (urjun) vividly illustrates the moon's waning phase, linking natural cycles to the concept of renewal and the orderly progression of time established by God.
